newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk ministry says scandal MP report incomplete.
newsitem.headline: Turk ministry says scandal MP report incomplete.

text.p: The Turkish Justice Ministry on Friday rejected as incomplete a prosecutor's report that could open the way for the prosecution of a government MP in a security scandal linking the state, police and underworld gangs.

State-run Anatolian news agency said the ministry returned the report back to the Ankara prosecutor. The report asked that the legal steps be taken to lift deputy Mehmet Agar's parliamentary immunity.

Agar, who quit as interior minister in November over the scandal, was accused this week of having signed a false police identity document for a fugitive gangster allegedly used by officials to kill Turkey's political opponents.

The scandal broke on November 3 when a truck collided with a car carrying a government MP who heads an anti-guerrilla Kurdish militia, a wanted gangster and a leading policeman. Only the government MP survived.
